summary: The global marketing team is executing a China-first strategy, with Asia Start and Intelligent China as top priorities, while managing urgent email lockouts and finalizing the knowledge website redesign.
summaryDetail: The team has pivoted to prioritize China-based programs—Asia Start and Intelligent China—for search/AI visibility, putting US partnerships on hold, and is now moving into implementation by drafting target prompts and auditing conversion tracking. This week, immediate attention is needed to resolve Outlook account lockouts across all devices and to schedule a working session for final feedback on the knowledge website redesign, which will keep the two-menu structure and integrate BCI/BSI indices. Looking ahead, key deliverables include sending updated Asia Start reports to European colleagues, planning video strategy, and preparing for the Nov 13 European Chamber event with panelist confirmations and a UNICON 2028 letter for the Dean. Additionally, the AACSB Global Impact Award 2027 application requires review, and the Berkeley program may be added as a third priority in the audit phase.

decisions.text: Re-login all email accounts on every device to resolve repeated lockouts.
Remove the standalone videos section; videos will be dispersed by topic across the site.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge menu and School menu) at the top.
Bring the BCI/BSI indices banner into the knowledge section, similar to the school homepage.
Do not add a stock-market-style ticker at the very top of the homepage.
Use Joseph's editorial layout as inspiration for showing more articles, not to be followed exactly.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China as top two programs to promote; US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) on hold initially.
Berkeley program to be considered as a possible third priority and included in the audit phase.
Pursue Holly Lei (Covestro China) as first-choice panelist, with Raphael (Sanofi) as fallback, for the Nov 13 European Chamber event
